text:
Maria G: quick heads-up — during the private deploy smoke run we noticed unexpected egress from the model-worker pods to metadata endpoints. also spotted a medium CVE in the keystore helper lib. need to discuss RBAC changes + audit retention + KMS wrapping for on-prem. who can triage?
Alex P: I can take the keystore/CVE triage. can you paste the vuln ID and the pod logs?
Maria G: CVE-2026-0421 (third-party key helper). logs are clipped but gist: `GET http://169.254.169.254` from model-worker when env var KMS_FALLBACK=1 was set. not sure why fallback allowed raw metadata access.
Jamal S: that's the netpol gap — our NetworkPolicy default for the tenant namespace allows outbound to CIDR 169.254.0.0/16 via a legacy rule. we tightened it last week but that namespace missed the label.
Tim O: we should avoid broad RBAC changes that break customer keys. proposal: enforce a canary RBAC role in `priv-keystore-canary` ns, test KMS wrapped decrypt, then roll across. no cluster-admin changes yet.
Sophie L: audit question — compliance wants 2 years for key ops logs for regulated installs. but on-prem storage makes that heavy. can we do compressed offload to S3-compatible object store and keep hashes in local DB?
Alex P: yes — plan: rotate keystore helper to patched version, enable strict KMS wrapping, add an allowlist of metadata IPs only for control-plane nodes, and add audit forwarder to object-store with daily manifests.
sre-bot: rotation-runbook triggered by @Alex P — job: keystore-patch-rotate-1719 started. see /ops/jobs/1719
Maria G: network policy snippet that Jamal suggested — please review:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-metadata-egress
  namespace: tenant-prod-123
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-worker
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 172.16.0.0/12
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 192.168.0.0/16
    # no 169.254/16 entry
```
Jamal S: lgtm, but add explicit egress to KMS proxy IP and to the metrics endpoint. otherwise healthchecks fail.
Tim O: for RBAC, use a scoped rolebinding:
```
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: keystore-access
  namespace: priv-keystore-canary
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
bind to serviceaccount `keystore-agent-canary` only.
Sophie L: audit retention action item: create policy to offload daily gzipped audits to customer-object-store and keep 90d local, 2y remote. include HMAC manifests for tamper-evidence.
Alex P: I'll open a PR for the keystore patch + RBAC+netpol. @Maria G can you run the canary and report the validation checks? checklist for canary: `decrypt -> metrics -> no 169.254 hits -> audit forwarded`
Maria G: starting canary now. will post results.
ops-bot: Canaries: priv-keystore-canary started (id: ck-884). expected run 3m.
Maria G: canary finished: decrypt OK, metrics OK, audit forwarded OK, still one perf pod retried when egress denied (known noncritical). no 169.254 requests.
Alex P: great — next steps: 1) merge patch PR  (assign @Alex P) 2) schedule rolling canary across 5 tenants 3) run tabletop incident sim for kms/fallback 4/28 @10am — Sophie please own the sim?
Sophie L: I can own the tabletop. I'll draft scenario including a simulated key compromise and log integrity check.
Jamal S: I'll update the networkpolicy-enforcer job to detect unlabeled namespaces and open a remediation PR.
Tim O: document the RBAC rollback steps in runbook (how to rebind old roles) and add automated smoke after each rollout.
Maria G: thanks all. filing follow-up issues: #SEC-872 (keystore patch), #SEC-873 (netpol remediation), #SEC-874 (audit offload). tagging compliance for retention sign-off. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: ticket created #SEC-872 #SEC-873 #SEC-874
Maria G: closing loop here — quick postmortem to follow once PRs merge. if anything pops up ping here. :thumbsup:
